author: sonnet-research-worker (development-cycle-2026-09-15)
purpose: Frozen typed fixtures distinguishing valid_at (when a claim was true in the world) from known_at (when the system learned it), for a state(valid_at=T, known_at=K) query that does not yet exist in physis-core. Do not edit case data after a validator run is cited in a report; add new cases with new ids instead.

status_vocabulary.SUPPORTED: at least one visible, time-applicable supporting item and no visible, time-applicable contradicting item
status_vocabulary.CONTRADICTED: at least one visible, time-applicable contradicting item (contradicting takes precedence over supporting when both are applicable)
status_vocabulary.UNKNOWN_TIME: no visible, time-applicable dated item, but at least one visible item whose valid time is explicitly unknown -- an abstention, not a negative
status_vocabulary.NO_BELIEF: no visible evidence bears on the subject at all (nothing known_at<=K, or the subject does not exist yet)

interval_semantics: half-open [valid_from, valid_until): valid_at == valid_from is inside the window, valid_at == valid_until is outside it. This matches physis-core/src/temporal.rs TemporalValidity::is_valid_at (from <= when && when < until). null valid_from = open at the start of time; null valid_until = open-ended / still valid.
visibility_rule: an evidence item is visible at known_at=K iff item.known_at <= K. If item.supersedes names another item's id, the superseded item is excluded from visibility once the superseding item itself is visible (visibility gates the correction, not the correction's own valid window).

cases.subject: boiler-7:pressure-reading-jan
cases.notes: Reproduces the Day-4 acceptance gate literally: 'a January reading learned in March is absent from a February knowledge query but available to an April query about January.'

evidence.claim: On 2026-01-15 boiler-7 read 42 psi, within the 45 psi limit.

queries.why: the February query predates when e1 was recorded (known_at=March); the reading is invisible even though the January event already happened
the April query is after e1 was recorded, and January 15 falls inside e1's valid window

cases.subject: reactor-3:temperature-below-70
cases.notes: Typed replacement for benchmarks/conatus/e77_temporal.py's prose-dates setup. All three evidence items are known by the same final known_at (mirrors E77's 'query after all evidence is in'); the three valid_at queries must return DIFFERENT statuses if the engine reads event time. This is E77's own falsification test, made executable against a typed oracle instead of CLI stdout regex.

evidence.claim: 2026-01-01: reactor-3 ran at 60C, below the 70C limit.
2026-06-01: reactor-3 ran at 80C, above the 70C limit.
2026-12-01: reactor-3 ran at 95C, above the 70C limit.

queries.why: January is inside e_jan's window and no contradicting item covers January
June is the exact instant e_jan's window closes (excluded, half-open) and e_jun's window opens (included)
December is inside e_dec's open-ended window

cases.known_bad_expectation: a known_at-only replay (ignores valid_at, uses only visibility-by-K) sees all three items visible and must return the SAME status (CONTRADICTED, since a contradicting item is visible) for q_jan, q_jun and q_dec alike -- reproducing E77's measured defect that replay at different timestamps does not track what the evidence is ABOUT.

cases.subject: reactor-3:temperature-below-70:arrival-order
cases.notes: Same three evidence items as T02, but known_at is assigned in reverse arrival order (e_dec known before e_jun before e_jan). Retrospective queries at the FINAL known_at must match T02 exactly (arrival order must not change the world-state answer once everything is in). Intermediate known_at queries are allowed, and expected, to differ from the forward arm -- that is not a bug.

evidence.claim: 2026-01-01: reactor-3 ran at 60C, below the 70C limit.
2026-06-01: reactor-3 ran at 80C, above the 70C limit.
2026-12-01: reactor-3 ran at 95C, above the 70C limit.

queries.why: final retrospective answer must equal T02.q_jan regardless of arrival order
final retrospective answer must equal T02.q_jun regardless of arrival order
at this intermediate known_at only e_dec is visible (reverse order), and e_dec's window does not cover June -- legitimately different from the forward arm's state at an equivalent step

cases.subject: valve-12:open
cases.notes: Mirrors physis-core/src/temporal.rs test a_window_closed_by_weak_evidence_is_corrected_by_better_evidence: a first, worse guess about when a claim stopped being true is later narrowed by better evidence. Modeled here as an explicit supersede rather than in-place mutation, since the fixture format has no notion of editing a record after the fact.

evidence.claim: Valve-12 was open from March to November (first estimate, based on the November inspection alone).
Correction: maintenance logs show valve-12 was actually closed by July; the November estimate over-ran the window.

queries.why: before the correction is known, the wide (wrong) window is still the best available belief
after the correction, August falls in the gap the correction opened up (valve already closed by July) -- neither evidence item is applicable, and this must not be silently reported as still SUPPORTED
May is still inside the corrected window

cases.subject: sensor-4:calibration-ok
cases.notes: A correction that does not just narrow an interval but reverses the claim: the original record said the sensor was fine; the correction says it was miscalibrated the whole time. known_at gating must still hold -- pre-correction queries see the wrong belief, this is expected and not a defect in the fixture.

evidence.claim: Sensor-4 was correctly calibrated all year.
Audit finds sensor-4 was miscalibrated from 2026-01-01 onward; retroactive correction.

queries.why: before the audit is known, the (wrong) calibrated belief is the honest historical answer at that known_at
same valid_at, later known_at: the retroactive correction now applies and flips the answer -- this is the point of separating the two axes

cases.subject: line-2:rattling-noise-reported
cases.notes: The only evidence for this subject has no extractable world time (an operator mentioned it in passing with no date). This must surface as an explicit abstention (UNKNOWN_TIME), never silently as NO_BELIEF (which would say nothing was ever reported) and never as a false SUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED at an arbitrary T.

evidence.claim: An operator mentioned line-2 has been making a rattling noise, no date given.

queries.why: there is relevant evidence, but no valid_at query can be honestly answered SUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED without a world time to place it at
before the report itself is even known, there is nothing to abstain about -- NO_BELIEF is correct here, not UNKNOWN_TIME

cases.subject: line-2:rattling-noise-vs-dated-inspection
cases.notes: An undated complaint coexists with a dated, applicable inspection record. Inside the dated record's window the dated evidence must win outright; outside every dated window the undated evidence must still surface as UNKNOWN_TIME rather than being dropped.

evidence.claim: An operator mentioned line-2 has been making a rattling noise, no date given.
2026-08-01 scheduled inspection: line-2 running within spec, no rattle observed, valid through the next inspection cycle.

queries.why: a dated, applicable, contradicting-to-the-complaint record inside its own window wins over an undated item
once outside the inspection's window, only the undated complaint remains visible and relevant -- must not silently disappear

cases.subject: permit-9:valid-window
cases.notes: valid_at exactly equal to valid_from must be INSIDE the window (half-open, start inclusive).

queries.why: start instant is inside the window
one second before the window opens, the permit is not yet valid

cases.subject: permit-9:valid-window
cases.notes: valid_at exactly equal to valid_until must be OUTSIDE the window (half-open, end exclusive) -- the classic off-by-one trap.

queries.why: the end instant itself is already expired
one second before expiry, still valid

cases.subject: policy-3:in-effect
cases.notes: valid_until=null means still valid arbitrarily far into the future; valid_from=null means valid since before any recorded evidence.

evidence.claim: Policy-3 took effect 2026-01-01 and has not been rescinded.

queries.why: an open-ended valid_until must not silently expire
